Let the original square have side length \(4\). After the two folds, the folded square has side length \(2\).

The two cuts are made along the midlines of the folded square, so when unfolded, these cuts appear one quarter of the original side from each edge. Thus the original square is divided into a \(3\times 3\) grid with side lengths

\[
1,\ 2,\ 1
\]

in both directions.

The pieces are therefore:
- Four corner pieces of size \(1\times 1\), which are squares.
- One central piece of size \(2\times 2\), which is a square.
- Four side pieces of size \(1\times 2\) or \(2\times 1\), which are not squares.

Hence the number of square pieces is

\[
4+1=5.
\]

\boxed{5}
\]
